examples.en: I took a boat and visited a small rocky island.
There is a rocky island in the middle of the sea.

examples.ko: 저 바위섬에는 갈매기가 아주 많이 살아요.
examples.en: A lot of seagulls live on that rocky island.

examples.ko: 파도가 높아서 바위섬 근처로는 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The waves are high, so we can't go near the rocky island.

examples.ko: 바위섬 위로 해가 떠오르는 모습이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The sun rising over the rocky island looks really beautiful.
Do you know where the rocky island in the photo is?

explain: 사람이 사는 큰 섬보다는 바다 위에 불쑥 솟은 작은 섬을 떠올릴 때 써요. 풍경, 낚시, 바닷새 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It brings to mind a small island that juts out of the sea rather than a large inhabited one. It often appears when people talk about scenery, fishing and seabirds.

examples.en: A small flower bloomed in a crack in the rocks.
The crab slipped right into a crack in the rocks.

examples.ko: 열쇠가 바위틈에 끼어서 꺼낼 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The key is stuck in a crack in the rocks and I can't get it out.
Clear water flows out from between the rocks.

examples.ko: 아이들이 바위틈을 들여다보며 작은 물고기를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The children peered into the cracks in the rocks and looked for small fish.
When it rains, water collects in the cracks in the rocks.

explain: '바위 틈'처럼 띄지 않고 한 단어로 써요. 꽃이 피거나 작은 동물이 숨는 장면, 물이 새어 나오는 장면에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is written as one word, not '바위 틈'. It often appears in scenes where a flower grows, a small animal hides, or water seeps out.

examples.en: The legs of these pants are too wide.
I'd like to take the legs in a little. Is that possible?
Wide-leg jeans are in style these days.
The legs are narrow, so it's uncomfortable when I sit.
I had the legs taken in by about a hand's width at the tailor.
The length looks short compared to the width of the legs.

explain: 바지에서 다리가 들어가는 부분의 넓이를 말할 때 써요. 옷 가게나 수선집에서 '바지통을 줄이다/늘리다'처럼 자주 말해요. 다리 부분 자체는 '바짓가랑이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to how wide the leg part of the pants is. In clothing shops and tailors people say '바지통을 줄이다/늘리다'. The leg part itself is called '바짓가랑이'.

examples.ko: 아이가 제 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 놓지 않아요.
examples.en: The child is holding on to my pant leg and won't let go.
My pant legs got completely wet because of the rain.
I rolled up my pant legs and stepped into the stream.
Your pant legs are covered in dirt.
The excited puppy kept tugging at my pant leg with its teeth.
The pant legs are so long that I keep stepping on them.

explain: 바지에서 한쪽 다리가 들어가는 부분이에요. 아이가 매달리거나 비에 젖는 장면에서 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '가랑이'라고도 하지만 몸의 다리 사이를 가리킬 수도 있어서, 옷 이야기에서는 '바짓가랑이'가 더 분명해요.

phrases.example: 취직 좀 시켜 달라고 사장님 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 늘어졌어요.
phrases.en: I clung to the boss's pant leg and begged him to give me a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체면을 가리지 않고 끈질기게 부탁하거나 매달릴 때 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for begging or clinging on persistently without caring about dignity.
phrases.en_equiv: to cling to someone and beg; to hang on and plead

explain_en: It is the part of the pants that covers one leg, and it often appears when a child clings on or the pants get wet. It can be shortened to '가랑이', but that can also mean the crotch of the body, so '바짓가랑이' is clearer when talking about clothes.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 마지막 주자에게 바통을 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our class passed the baton to the last runner.
We dropped the baton, so our team lost.

examples.ko: 바통 터치가 아주 부드러워서 기록이 좋았어요.
examples.en: The baton pass was very smooth, so our time was good.

examples.ko: 선배에게서 바통을 이어받아 새 책임자가 됐어요.
examples.en: I took over from my senior and became the new person in charge.
The baton slipped out of my hand in the relay.
If you run without a baton, it isn't a relay.

explain: 계주에서 쓰는 막대지만 일을 넘겨주고 받는 이야기에도 많이 써요. '바통 터치'는 말 그대로 넘겨주는 동작이면서 '업무 인수인계'의 뜻으로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 이번 달부터 제가 팀장 일의 바통을 이어받았어요.
phrases.en: From this month, I took over the team leader's work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞사람이 하던 일이나 책임을 이어서 맡을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when you take over work or responsibility that someone before you was handling.
phrases.en_equiv: to take over the baton; to pick up the torch

explain_en: It is the stick used in relay races, but people also use it when talking about handing work over to someone. '바통 터치' is the actual handoff and is also used for handing over duties.

examples.en: When the show ended, the audience gave it a big round of applause.
Applause burst out after the speech ended.
He stepped down from the stage amid applause.
The rookie singer received great applause.
Applause poured in for the young performer.
I was moved by the applause and started to cry.

explain: 그냥 '박수'보다 크고 칭찬이 담긴 환호의 느낌이에요. '받다, 보내다, 쏟아지다, 터져 나오다'와 함께 써요. 말할 때는 '박수를 많이 받았어요'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It feels bigger than plain '박수', with cheering and praise. It pairs with verbs like 받다, 보내다, 쏟아지다 and 터져 나오다. In casual speech people often just say '박수를 많이 받았어요'.

examples.en: Grandma took a mint candy out of her bag and gave it to me.
When you eat a mint candy, your mouth feels cool.

examples.ko: 목이 아플 때 박하사탕 하나를 물고 있어요.
examples.en: When my throat hurts, I keep a mint candy in my mouth.

examples.ko: 이 박하사탕은 너무 달고 향이 강해요.
examples.en: This mint candy is too sweet and the scent is strong.

examples.ko: 식당 계산대에 박하사탕이 한가득 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a pile of mint candies at the restaurant's cash register.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 먹던 박하사탕이 갑자기 생각나요.
examples.en: I suddenly remembered the mint candy I ate as a kid.

explain: 박하 향이 나는 하얗거나 투명한 사탕이에요. 식당에서 계산한 뒤 입가심으로 주는 경우가 많아서 그런 장면에서 자주 나와요. '민트 사탕'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a white or clear candy with a mint flavor. Restaurants often hand it out after you pay to freshen your mouth, so it shows up in that scene a lot. People also say '민트 사탕'.

examples.en: I wiped the floor and now it shines.

examples.ko: 아이가 반들반들 닳은 돌을 주워 왔어요.
examples.en: The child picked up a smooth, worn stone.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed.
The wooden handle, used for a long time, is smooth and shiny.
I polished the apple until it was shiny and then ate it.

examples.ko: 새로 산 차가 햇빛에 반들반들 빛나요.
examples.en: The newly bought car gleams in the sunlight.

explain: 표면이 매끄럽고 윤이 날 때 써요. '번들번들'은 기름기가 있어 번지르르한 느낌이 들 때가 있고, '반들반들'은 깨끗하고 매끈한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Used when a surface is smooth and shiny. '번들번들' can feel greasy or slick, while '반들반들' feels clean and sleek.

examples.ko: 하향 곡선을 그리던 판매량이 이번 달에 겨우 반등했어요.
examples.en: Sales that had been on a downward curve finally rebounded this month.

examples.ko: 매출이 반등할 조짐이 있어요? 아직 확실하지는 않지만 주문이 조금 늘었어요.
examples.en: Are there signs that sales will rebound? It's not certain yet, but orders have increased a little.

examples.ko: 어제 크게 떨어진 주가가 오늘은 반등하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The stock price that fell sharply yesterday started to rebound today.

examples.ko: 환율이 반등하면 여행 계획을 다시 생각해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: If the exchange rate rebounds, we'll have to rethink our travel plans.

examples.ko: 경기가 반등하려면 신제품이 먼저 나와야 해요.
examples.en: For business to rebound, new products have to come out first.
My grades dropped but rebounded on the final exam, so I'm happy.

explain: 한동안 내려가던 것이 다시 올라갈 때 써요. 주가, 매출, 환율, 성적 이야기에 어울리고, 처음부터 오르는 것에는 그냥 '오르다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when something that had been falling for a while goes back up. It suits talk about stock prices, sales, exchange rates and grades. For something that simply rises from the start, just use '오르다'.

examples.en: I saw fireflies for the first time on a summer night in the countryside.
Fireflies twinkled among the grass.

examples.ko: 깨끗한 개울가에서만 반딧불이를 볼 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can only see fireflies by clean streams.
The kids took part in a firefly experience event.
Fireflies give off light from their tails.
The firefly lights looked like stars.

explain: '반딧불이'는 곤충 이름이고, '이'까지가 한 단어라서 '반딧불이가', '반딧불이를'처럼 조사가 붙으면 '이'가 겹쳐 보여요. '반딧불'은 그 곤충이 내는 불빛을 가리켜요. 곤충은 '개똥벌레'라고도 불러요.
explain_en: This is the name of the insect, and the final '이' is part of the word, so with particles it looks like '반딧불이가' or '반딧불이를', with the '이' appearing twice. '반딧불' refers to the light the insect gives off. The insect is also called '개똥벌레'.

examples.en: I'm really happy to have met my lifelong partner.
He calls his wife the companion of his life.

examples.ko: 좋은 반려자는 힘들 때 곁에 있어 줘요.
examples.en: A good partner stays by your side when times are hard.

examples.ko: 반려자와 함께 늙어 가는 것이 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to grow old together with my partner.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 서로에게 평생 반려자가 되겠다고 약속했어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, they promised to be each other's lifelong partners.

examples.ko: 여행에서는 마음 맞는 반려자가 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: On a trip, it's nice to have a like-minded companion.

explain: 주로 배우자를 따뜻하게 부를 때 쓰는 말로, '인생의 반려자'라는 짝이 가장 흔해요. 일상 대화에서는 '남편/아내'라고 하고, 축사나 편지, 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mainly a warm way to refer to a spouse, and '인생의 반려자' (life partner) is the most common pairing. In daily talk people say '남편' or '아내', while this appears more in congratulatory speeches, letters and writing.

examples.ko: 잘 구운 햄버거에 달걀 반숙을 올려 아침으로 먹었어요.
examples.en: I put a soft-cooked egg on a well-grilled hamburger and had it for breakfast.
Do you like your eggs soft-cooked or hard-cooked?

examples.ko: 반숙 노른자가 밥에 흘러서 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The runny yolk of a soft-cooked egg flows onto the rice and makes it tastier.
I only eat eggs cooked soft.
I put a soft-cooked egg in the ramen.

examples.ko: 반숙은 시간이 조금만 길어져도 완숙이 돼요.
examples.en: A soft-cooked egg becomes hard-cooked if the time runs just a little longer.

explain: 달걀을 노른자가 덜 익게 삶거나 부칠 때 써요. 반대말은 '완숙'이고, 식당에서는 '반숙 프라이'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Used when an egg is boiled or fried so the yolk stays runny. The opposite is '완숙', and restaurants say things like '반숙 프라이'.

examples.ko: 길이 부드러운 반원을 그리며 휘어 있어요.
examples.en: The road curves in a gentle semicircle.
The students sat in a semicircle in front of the teacher.
Try drawing a semicircle with a compass.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 반원 모양의 터널이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a semicircle-shaped tunnel under the bridge.
I cut the cake into a half-circle shape.
The diameter of a semicircle is the same as that of the circle.

explain: 원을 반으로 나눈 모양이에요. 의자 배치나 도형 문제에 자주 나와요. 모양을 말할 때는 '반달 모양'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the shape you get when you cut a circle in half. It often comes up in seating arrangements and geometry problems. For the shape, people also say '반달 모양' (half-moon shape).

examples.en: I draw a circle with a radius of 5 centimeters.

examples.ko: 원의 반지름 구하는 문제가 시험에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A problem about finding the radius of a circle came up on the test.
Half of the diameter is the radius.

examples.ko: 반지름을 두 배로 늘리면 넓이는 네 배가 돼요.
examples.en: If you double the radius, the area becomes four times as large.
You open the compass to the length of the radius and draw a circle.
What is the radius of this plate?

explain: '지름'과 짝으로 같이 외워 두면 좋아요. 수학에서는 '반지름' 대신 '반경'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is useful to learn it as a pair with '지름' (diameter). In math you may also see '반경' used for it.

examples.en: I buy side dish ingredients at the market.
I don't have good ingredients for tonight's side dishes.

examples.ko: 마트에 가서 반찬거리 좀 사 올게요.
examples.en: I'll go to the mart and pick up some ingredients for side dishes.

examples.ko: 텃밭에서 따 온 채소로 반찬거리를 마련했어요.
examples.en: I got side dish ingredients ready with vegetables picked from the garden.
What would be good for the side dish ingredients?
It's cheap and fresh, so it's perfect for making side dishes.

explain: 이미 만들어진 반찬이 아니라 반찬을 만들 재료를 말해요. 줄여서 '찬거리'라고도 하고, 시장이나 마트에서 장 볼 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the ingredients for making side dishes, not the finished dishes themselves. It is also shortened to '찬거리', and people use it when shopping at the market or mart.

examples.en: I worked at one workplace for half of my life.
My father has done nothing but farm for half of his life.

examples.ko: 반평생이 지나서야 제 꿈을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Only after half my life had passed did I realize what my dream was.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 우리 가족이 반평생 지켜 온 곳이에요.
examples.en: This shop is a place our family has kept going for half a lifetime.

examples.ko: 반평생 동안 고향을 떠난 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I haven't left my hometown in half my life.
I heard they donated the money they had saved for half their life.

explain: 정확히 몇 년이라는 뜻보다 '아주 오랜 세월'이라는 느낌으로 써요. 어른이 자기 삶을 돌아보며 말할 때 자주 나와요. 평생 전체를 말할 때는 '평생'을 써요.
explain_en: It conveys 'a very long time' rather than an exact number of years, and adults often use it when looking back on their lives. For the whole of a life, use '평생'.

examples.en: It's easy to develop a rebellious streak during puberty.
The more nagging I hear, the more my defiance just grows.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 반항심 때문에 일부러 반대로 행동해요.
examples.en: That child deliberately does the opposite out of defiance.
I held back my urge to rebel and followed the teacher's words.
Out of a little rebelliousness, I went to school late.
Rebelliousness is a natural feeling in the process of growing up.

explain: '반항'은 행동이고 '반항심'은 그 마음이에요. 보통 '생기다, 들다, 커지다'와 함께 쓰고 사춘기 아이 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '반항' is the act of defying, while '반항심' is the feeling behind it. It usually goes with 생기다, 들다 and 커지다, and often appears in talk about teenagers.

examples.en: He was a well-known rebel at school.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 세상에 맞서는 반항아예요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie is a rebel who stands up to the world.
I was a rebel when I was young, but now I'm well-behaved.

examples.ko: 반항아 같은 모습이 매력적이라는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people find a rebellious look attractive.

examples.ko: 우리 막내는 요즘 완전히 반항아가 됐어요.
examples.en: Our youngest has turned into a total rebel lately.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 반항아 이미지로 인기를 끌었어요.
examples.en: That singer became popular with a rebel image.

explain: 꾸짖는 말로만 쓰지 않고, '반항아 이미지'처럼 멋있고 개성 있는 사람을 말할 때도 있어요. 사람을 바로 앞에서 부를 때는 기분이 상할 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It isn't only a scolding word. It can also describe someone cool and individualistic, as in '반항아 이미지'. Be careful calling someone this to their face, as it may offend them.

examples.ko: 사춘기 아들이 요즘 반항적인 말투를 써요.
examples.en: My teenage son uses a defiant tone these days.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어른들 앞에서 반항적으로 행동해요.
examples.en: That child acts defiantly in front of adults.

examples.ko: 아이가 반항적일 때는 먼저 이야기를 들어 주세요.
examples.en: When a child is rebellious, listen to what they have to say first.
The song lyrics are a little rebellious.
He isn't rebellious at all and is very gentle.
The rebellious character is the charm of this drama.

explain: '반항적인 태도/말투/눈빛'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 많이 써요. '반항적이다'로 서술할 수도 있어요. 사람 자체를 가리킬 때는 '반항아'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is most often used to modify a noun that follows, as in '반항적인 태도/말투/눈빛'. You can also use it as a predicate, '반항적이다'. For the person himself, say '반항아'.

examples.en: My cheeks are frozen red from the cold.
The sunset has turned the sky red.
Bright red apples are hanging on the tree.
Your face is red from the sun.
Your eyes were red, so I asked if you had been crying.
The baby's cheeks are rosy and cute.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 작고 은은한 붉은색에 어울리고, 큰 것이나 짙은 느낌은 '벌겋다'와 짝을 이뤄요. ㅎ 불규칙이라 '발개요, 발간, 발갛게'처럼 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It suits a small or soft shade of red, more delicate than '빨갛다'. Its larger counterpart is '벌겋다'. It is an irregular ㅎ adjective, so it changes like 발개요, 발간, 발갛게.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 문을 향해 발길질을 했어요.
examples.en: The child got angry and kicked at the door.
I kicked hard at the ball.

examples.ko: 자는 동안 발길질이 심해서 이불이 다 벗겨졌어요.
examples.en: I kicked a lot in my sleep, so the blanket came all the way off.
The puppy flails its hind legs as if kicking.

examples.ko: 아기가 기저귀를 갈 때 계속 발길질해요.
examples.en: The baby keeps kicking while I change the diaper.
You shouldn't kick around carelessly just because you're angry.

explain: '발로 차다'보다 반복되거나 거친 느낌이 있어요. 아기가 버둥거리거나 화가 나서 마구 차는 장면에 어울려요. 손으로 치는 건 '주먹질'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels more repeated or rough than '발로 차다'. It fits a baby flailing or someone kicking wildly out of anger. Hitting with fists is called '주먹질'.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 뼈가 연해서 발라내지 않고 먹어도 돼요.
examples.en: This fish has soft bones, so you can eat it without removing them.

examples.ko: 아이를 위해 생선 가시를 꼼꼼히 발라냈어요.
examples.en: I carefully picked the bones out of the fish for the child.
I take the bones out of the chicken and stir-fry only the meat.
Peeling off the shrimp shells is a hassle.

examples.ko: 가시를 발라내 주시면 더 잘 먹을 것 같아요.
examples.en: If you pick out the bones for me, I think I'll eat better.
I bought only meat with the rib bones taken out.

explain: 뼈, 가시, 껍데기를 떼어 내고 먹을 살만 남길 때 써요. 생선, 고기, 새우나 게에 어울리고, '생선 살을 발라 먹다'처럼 '발라'만 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Used when you remove bones, fish bones or shells and keep only the edible meat. It suits fish, meat, shrimp and crab, and people often use just '발라', as in '생선 살을 발라 먹다'.

examples.en: Working in step with my colleagues makes it much easier.
They released a new menu to keep up with the trend.

examples.ko: 학교와 부모님이 발맞추면 아이가 잘 자라요.
examples.en: When school and parents work together, the child grows well.

examples.ko: 달리기 연습할 때 발맞추는 게 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to keep in step when practicing running.

examples.ko: 세계 흐름에 발맞추려면 영어 공부가 필요해요.
examples.en: To keep pace with the world, you need to study English.
The team members couldn't coordinate, so the work got delayed.

explain: 발걸음을 같게 한다는 데서 나와서, 지금은 속도나 방향을 맞춘다는 비유로 많이 써요. '~에 발맞춰'가 자주 나오는 모양이고, 비슷한 말로 '보조를 맞추다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It comes from walking in step, and today it is mostly used figuratively for matching speed or direction. '~에 발맞춰' is a very common form, and '보조를 맞추다' is a similar expression.

examples.en: The amount of waste generated is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 먼지 발생량을 줄이려고 노력해요.
examples.en: This factory is trying to reduce the amount of dust it produces.
The amount generated varies by season.
The results of the survey on the amount generated were announced today.
If you cut down on packaging, the amount of plastic waste goes down too.

examples.ko: 집집마다 쓰레기 발생량에 따라 봉투 값을 내요.
examples.en: Each household pays for bags according to how much waste it produces.

explain: 쓰레기, 먼지, 이산화탄소처럼 '나오는 양'을 말할 때 써요. 환경 뉴스에 자주 나오고 '늘다, 줄이다, 감소하다'와 함께 써요. 비율은 '발생률'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for the amount of things that come out, like waste, dust or carbon dioxide. It often appears in environmental news with verbs such as 늘다, 줄이다 and 감소하다. The ratio is called '발생률'.

examples.ko: 이 병의 발생률은 해마다 낮아지고 있어요.
examples.en: The incidence of this disease is falling every year.

examples.ko: 사고 발생률을 줄이려고 안전 교육을 해요.
examples.en: We hold safety training to reduce the accident rate.
The rate of colds is high in winter.
The difference in incidence rates between regions is quite big.
The number of reports is small compared to the occurrence rate.
They say the rate of side effects has also gone down.

explain: '발생량'은 나온 양이고 '발생률'은 전체에서 일어나는 비율이에요. 사고, 질병, 불량처럼 얼마나 자주 일어나는지 말할 때 쓰고, [발쌩뉼]로 소리 나요.
explain_en: '발생량' is the amount that occurred, while '발생률' is the proportion of occurrence out of the whole. It is used for how often accidents, diseases or defects happen, and it is pronounced [발쌩뉼].

examples.en: Please offer lots of constructive opinions.

examples.ko: 서로 싸우지 말고 발전적으로 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's not fight and talk in a constructive way.

examples.ko: 발전적이지 않은 비판은 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Criticism that isn't constructive doesn't help.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 발전적이라서 참여할 때마다 배워요.
examples.en: That group is productive, so I learn something every time I take part.

examples.ko: 더 발전적인 방향으로 이야기를 이끌어 보세요.
examples.en: Try steering the conversation in a more productive direction.
Was this discussion productive?

explain: 지금보다 나아지는 방향이라는 느낌으로 의견, 토론, 관계, 태도를 꾸밀 때 써요. 보통 '발전적인 + 명사'로 나오고, '건설적인'과 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It carries the sense of heading toward improvement, and describes opinions, discussions, relationships and attitudes. It usually appears as '발전적인 + noun', and is used much like '건설적인' (constructive).

examples.en: The full moon is up, so the night road is bright.
A cat jumped out on the night road and startled me.
A young child wandering the night streets alone, will they be okay?

examples.ko: 우리는 어두운 밤길을 나란히 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: We walked slowly side by side along the dark night road.
You have to be careful driving at night.
If it ends late, the night road will be scary, so I'll take you home.

explain: 밤에 걷거나 운전하는 길이라서 어둡고 위험하다는 느낌으로 자주 써요. '밤길을 걷다', '밤길 조심하세요'처럼 말하고, 헤어질 때 하는 인사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Because it is a road you walk or drive on at night, it often carries a feeling of darkness and danger. People say things like '밤길을 걷다', and '밤길 조심하세요' is a common farewell.

examples.en: A big chestnut tree stands on the mountain path.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 밤나무 아래에서 밤을 주워요.
examples.en: When autumn comes, we pick up chestnuts under the chestnut tree.

examples.ko: 할아버지 밭 뒤에 밤나무 몇 그루가 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few chestnut trees behind Grandfather's field.

examples.ko: 밤나무 꽃은 초여름에 피고 냄새가 독특해요.
examples.en: Chestnut blossoms bloom in early summer and have a distinctive smell.

examples.ko: 이 밤나무는 백 년도 더 됐대요.
examples.en: I heard this chestnut tree is over a hundred years old.
A chestnut burr fell from the chestnut tree.

explain: '밤(night)'과 '밤(chestnut)'은 소리가 같아요. '밤나무'는 열매 밤이 열리는 나무라서 헷갈릴 일이 없지만, '밤이 맛있다' 같은 문장은 앞뒤 말을 보고 뜻을 구분해요.
explain_en: '밤' meaning night and '밤' meaning chestnut sound the same. '밤나무' is the tree that bears chestnuts, so it is not confusing, but in a sentence like '밤이 맛있다' you tell the meaning from the context.

examples.ko: 우리 걸어서 가요. 밤바람이 시원해서 좋지 않아요?
examples.en: Let's walk. Isn't the night breeze nice and cool?
The night wind is quite cold today.

examples.ko: 창문을 열면 밤바람을 맞으며 잘 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you open the window, you can sleep with the night breeze on you.
My hair was blown about by the night wind.
I ate chicken by the Han River, enjoying the night air.
I think I caught a cold because of the night wind.

explain: '밤바람을 쐬다'가 가장 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 여름밤에는 시원하고 기분 좋은 느낌이고, 가을이나 겨울에는 차가운 느낌으로 말해요.
explain_en: '밤바람을 쐬다' (to get some night air) is the most common pairing. On summer nights it feels cool and pleasant, while in autumn or winter it feels cold.

examples.ko: 밤송이를 까 보니 속은 거의 다 벌레가 먹었어요.
examples.en: When I opened the chestnut burr, the inside was almost all eaten by worms.
My hand hurts because I was pricked by a chestnut burr.
Chestnut burrs drop with thuds in the autumn mountains.

examples.ko: 밤송이는 가시가 많아서 장갑을 껴야 해요.
examples.en: Chestnut burrs are very prickly, so you need to wear gloves.

examples.ko: 밤송이 안에 밤이 세 톨 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: There were three chestnuts inside the burr.
I can see chestnuts through the split-open burr.

explain: 밤을 감싼 가시 달린 껍질째를 부르는 말이에요. 그 안에 든 열매 하나는 '밤톨'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It names the whole prickly husk that wraps the chestnuts. A single nut inside is called a '밤톨'.

examples.en: This year the chestnuts are big and plump.
The squirrel ran off with a chestnut in its mouth.
Hail as big as chestnuts fell.

examples.ko: 밤톨 몇 개를 구워서 간식으로 먹었어요.
examples.en: I roasted a few chestnuts and ate them as a snack.

examples.ko: 가방 속에서 밤톨 하나가 굴러 나왔어요.
examples.en: A chestnut rolled out of the bag.
The baby's fist is small and cute like a chestnut.

explain: 밤송이 속에 든 밤 한 알을 가리켜요. 작고 단단한 것의 크기를 비유할 때 '밤톨만 하다', '밤톨 같다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a single chestnut inside the burr. To describe the size of something small and hard, people say '밤톨만 하다' or '밤톨 같다'.

examples.en: Please mix the rice evenly with the rice paddle.
Rice grains keep sticking to the rice paddle.

examples.ko: 밥주걱을 물에 적시면 밥이 덜 붙어요.
examples.en: If you wet the rice paddle, the rice sticks less.
I needed a new rice paddle, so I went to the mart.
I bought a rice paddle.
This rice paddle is plastic, so it's light and easy to use.

explain: 밥솥에서 밥을 푸고 섞을 때 쓰는 도구예요. 줄여서 그냥 '주걱'이라고도 하고, 국을 뜨는 도구는 '국자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the tool you use to scoop and mix rice from the rice cooker. It is often shortened to just '주걱', and the tool for ladling soup is called '국자'.

examples.en: My child fusses about food, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 밥투정하지 말고 한 숟가락만 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't fuss about your food; just try one spoonful.

examples.ko: 밥투정이 심한 동생 때문에 엄마가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Mom has a hard time because of my little sibling's picky fussing at meals.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 밥투정도 안 하고 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: My son eats well without any fussing about food.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 밥투정을 부리다 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I got scolded for fussing over my food.

examples.ko: 밥투정 부리는 아이에게 억지로 먹이지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't force-feed a child who is fussing about food.

explain: 반찬이 마음에 안 든다고 안 먹거나 칭얼댈 때 써요. '밥투정을 부리다/하다'로 말해요. '입이 짧다'는 원래 적게 먹거나 가리는 편이라는 뜻이어서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: Used when someone refuses to eat or whines because they dislike the dishes. You say '밥투정을 부리다/하다'. '입이 짧다' means someone naturally eats little or is picky, so it differs slightly.
